sanskrit: rātriyuddhe tadā ghore vartamāne sudāruṇe droṇam abhyadravan kruddhāḥ sahitāḥ pāṇḍusṛñjayāḥ
english: As the dreadful night-battle raged on, terrible beyond measure, the Pāṇḍavas and the Sṛñjayas, united and enraged, rushed upon Droṇa.

sanskrit: ye ye pramukhato rājan nyavartanta mahātmanaḥ tān sarvān vimukhāṃś cakre kāṃś cin ninye yamakṣayam
english: Whoever, O king, came to oppose that great-souled one face to face, all of these he turned away routed, and some of them he dispatched to the realm of Yama.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca tasmin praviṣṭe durdharṣe sṛñjayān amitaujasi amṛṣyamāṇe saṃrabdhe kā vo 'bhūd vai matis tadā
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When that unassailable one of boundless might had plunged among the Sṛñjayas, impatient and roused to fury, what then was your resolve?

sanskrit: duryodhanaṃ tathā putram uktvā śāstrātigaṃ mama yat prāviśad ameyātmā kiṃ pārthaḥ pratyapadyata
english: When that one of immeasurable spirit, having rebuked my son Duryodhana for transgressing the rules, had broken into the foe, how did Pārtha respond?

sanskrit: nihate saindhave vīre bhūriśravasi caiva hi yad abhyagān mahātejāḥ pāñcālān aparājitaḥ
english: After the heroic ruler of the Saindhavas had been slain, and Bhūriśravas too, how did that one of great splendor, unconquered, advance against the Pāñcālas?

sanskrit: kim amanyata durdharṣaḥ praviṣṭe śatrutāpane duryodhanaś ca kiṃ kṛtyaṃ prāptakālam amanyata
english: When that scorcher of foes, hard to assail, had broken in, what did Duryodhana think the fitting deed for the hour to be?

sanskrit: ke ca taṃ varadaṃ vīram anvayur dvijasattamam ke cāsya pṛṣṭhato 'gacchan vīrāḥ śūrasya yudhyataḥ ke purastād ayudhyanta nighnataḥ śātravān raṇe
english: Which heroes followed that boon-granting warrior, best of the twice-born? Which heroes went behind that valiant one as he fought? Which fought before him as he struck down his enemies in battle?

sanskrit: manye 'haṃ pāṇḍavān sarvān bhāradvājaśarārditān śiśire kampamānā vai kṛśā gāva ivābhibho
english: I think, my lord, that all the Pāṇḍavas, tormented by the shafts of Bhāradvāja, were trembling like gaunt cattle in the winter cold.

sanskrit: praviśya sa maheṣvāsaḥ pāñcālān arimardanaḥ kathaṃ nu puruṣavyāghraḥ pañcatvam upajagmivān
english: Having broken into the Pāñcālas, that mighty archer, crusher of foes, that tiger among men—how then did he meet his dissolution?

sanskrit: sarveṣu sainyeṣu ca saṃgateṣu; rātrau sameteṣu mahāratheṣu saṃloḍyamāneṣu pṛthagvidheṣu; ke vas tadānīṃ matimanta āsan
english: When all the armies had clashed together, and in the night the great chariot-warriors had met and the varied hosts were thrown into turmoil, who among you then kept their wits about them?

sanskrit: hatāṃś caiva viṣaktāṃś ca parābhūtāṃś ca śaṃsasi rathino virathāṃś caiva kṛtān yuddheṣu māmakān
english: You tell of my men—slain, beset, and overthrown, the chariot-warriors made chariotless in the fighting.

sanskrit: katham eṣāṃ tadā tatra pārthānām apalāyinām prakāśam abhavad rātrau kathaṃ kuruṣu saṃjaya
english: How then, Saṃjaya, did light come to these unflinching sons of Pṛthā there in the night, and how among the Kurus?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca rātriyuddhe tadā rājan vartamāne sudāruṇe droṇam abhyadravan rātrau pāṇḍavāḥ sahasainikāḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: As the night-battle raged on, O king, exceedingly terrible, the Pāṇḍavas with their soldiers rushed upon Droṇa in the dark.

sanskrit: tato droṇaḥ kekayāṃś ca dhṛṣṭadyumnasya cātmajān preṣayan mṛtyulokāya sarvān iṣubhir āśugaiḥ
english: Then Droṇa, with his swift-flying arrows, sent the Kekayas and the sons of Dhṛṣṭadyumna, every one of them, off to the realm of death.

sanskrit: tasya pramukhato rājan ye 'vartanta mahārathāḥ tān sarvān preṣayām āsa paralokāya bhārata
english: Whatever great chariot-warriors stood before him, O king, all of these, descendant of Bharata, he sent to the world beyond.

sanskrit: pramathnantaṃ tadā vīraṃ bhāradvājaṃ mahāratham abhyavartata saṃkruddhaḥ śibī rājan pratāpavān
english: Against that hero Bhāradvāja, the great chariot-warrior who was crushing all before him, the valorous Śibi, O king, advanced in wrath.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ saṃprekṣya pāṇḍavānāṃ mahāratham vivyādha daśabhir droṇaḥ sarvapāraśavaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Beholding that great chariot-warrior of the Pāṇḍavas bearing down upon him, Droṇa pierced him with ten shafts all made of steel.

sanskrit: taṃ śibiḥ prativivyādha triṃśatā niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ sārathiṃ cāsya bhallena smayamāno nyapātayat
english: Śibi pierced him in return with thirty sharpened shafts, and smiling, with a broad-headed arrow, struck down his charioteer.

sanskrit: tasya droṇo hayān hatvā sārathiṃ ca mahātmanaḥ athāsya saśirastrāṇaṃ śiraḥ kāyād apāharat
english: Then Droṇa, having slain the horses and the charioteer of that great-souled one, struck off his head, helmet and all, from his body.

sanskrit: kaliṅgānāṃ ca sainyena kaliṅgasya suto raṇe pūrvaṃ pitṛvadhāt kruddho bhīmasenam upādravat
english: Then the son of the Kaliṅga king, enraged at the earlier slaying of his father, charged upon Bhīmasena in battle with the army of the Kaliṅgas.

sanskrit: sa bhīmaṃ pañcabhir viddhvā punar vivyādha saptabhiḥ viśokaṃ tribhir ājaghne dhvajam ekena patriṇā
english: Having pierced Bhīma with five shafts, he wounded him again with seven, struck Viśoka with three, and his banner with a single feathered arrow.

sanskrit: kaliṅgānāṃ tu taṃ śūraṃ kruddhaṃ kruddho vṛkodaraḥ rathād ratham abhidrutya muṣṭinābhijaghāna ha
english: But Vṛkodara, enraged, leaping from chariot to chariot, smote that enraged hero of the Kaliṅgas with his fist.

sanskrit: tasya muṣṭihatasyājau pāṇḍavena balīyasā sarvāṇy asthīni sahasā prāpatan vai pṛthak pṛthak
english: Struck in battle by the fist of the mighty Pāṇḍava, all his bones at once fell apart, each from the other.

sanskrit: taṃ karṇo bhrātaraś cāsya nāmṛṣyanta mahārathāḥ te bhīmasenaṃ nārācair jaghnur āśīviṣopamaiḥ
english: Karṇa and that one's brothers, the great chariot-warriors, could not bear this; they struck Bhīmasena with iron shafts like venomous serpents.

sanskrit: tataḥ śatrurathaṃ tyaktvā bhīmo dhruvarathaṃ gataḥ dhruvaṃ cāsyantam aniśaṃ muṣṭinā samapothayat sa tathā pāṇḍuputreṇa balinā nihato 'patat
english: Then Bhīma, abandoning the enemy's chariot, sprang to Dhruva's car, and crushed with his fist Dhruva, who was loosing shafts without pause; thus struck down by the mighty son of Pāṇḍu, he fell.

sanskrit: taṃ nihatya mahārāja bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ jayarātarathaṃ prāpya muhuḥ siṃha ivānadat
english: Having slain him, O great king, the mighty Bhīmasena reached the chariot of Jayarāta and roared again and again like a lion.

sanskrit: jayarātam athākṣipya nadan savyena pāṇinā talena nāśayām āsa karṇasyaivāgrataḥ sthitam
english: Seizing Jayarāta then, roaring, with the flat of his left hand he destroyed him as he stood there before the very eyes of Karṇa.

sanskrit: karṇas tu pāṇḍave śaktiṃ kāñcanīṃ samavāsṛjat tatas tām eva jagrāha prahasan pāṇḍunandanaḥ
english: Karṇa then hurled a golden javelin at the Pāṇḍava, but the son of Pāṇḍu, laughing, caught that very weapon.

sanskrit: karṇāyaiva ca durdharṣaś cikṣepājau vṛkodaraḥ tām antarikṣe ciccheda śakunis tailapāyinā
english: And the unassailable Vṛkodara flung it back at Karṇa in the fray, but Śakuni cut it down in mid-air with an oil-honed shaft.

sanskrit: tatas tava sutā rājan bhīmasya ratham āvrajan mahatā śaravarṣeṇa chādayanto vṛkodaram
english: Then your sons, O king, advanced upon Bhīma's chariot, covering Vṛkodara with a mighty rain of arrows.

sanskrit: durmadasya tato bhīmaḥ prahasann iva saṃyuge sārathiṃ ca hayāṃś caiva śarair ninye yamakṣayam durmadas tu tato yānaṃ duṣkarṇasyāvapupluve
english: Then Bhīma, as if laughing in the combat, dispatched Durmada's charioteer and horses to the realm of Yama with his shafts; whereupon Durmada leapt onto the car of Duṣkarṇa.

sanskrit: tāv ekaratham ārūḍhau bhrātarau paratāpanau saṃgrāmaśiraso madhye bhīmaṃ dvāv abhyadhāvatām yathāmbupatimitrau hi tārakaṃ daityasattamam
english: Those two brothers, scorchers of foes, mounted upon a single chariot, both charged at Bhīma in the midst of the battle's van, as two friends of the lord of waters might charge Tāraka, foremost of the Daityas.

sanskrit: tatas tu durmadaś caiva duṣkarṇaś ca tavātmajau ratham ekaṃ samāruhya bhīmaṃ bāṇair avidhyatām
english: Then Durmada and Duṣkarṇa, your two sons, mounting upon a single chariot, pierced Bhīma with their arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ karṇasya miṣato drauṇer duryodhanasya ca kṛpasya somadattasya bāhlīkasya ca pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Then, before the watching eyes of Karṇa, of Drauṇi, of Duryodhana, of Kṛpa, of Somadatta, and of Bāhlika, the Pāṇḍava—

sanskrit: durmadasya ca vīrasya duṣkarṇasya ca taṃ ratham pādaprahāreṇa dharāṃ prāveśayad ariṃdamaḥ
english: —that tamer of foes drove the chariot of the heroes Durmada and Duṣkarṇa into the earth with a single stamp of his foot.

sanskrit: tataḥ sutau te balinau śūrau duṣkarṇadurmadau muṣṭināhatya saṃkruddho mamarda caraṇena ca
english: Then, enraged, he struck your two mighty, valiant sons Duṣkarṇa and Durmada with his fist and ground them down beneath his foot.

sanskrit: tato hāhākṛte sainye dṛṣṭvā bhīmaṃ nṛpābruvan rudro 'yaṃ bhīmarūpeṇa dhārtarāṣṭreṣu gṛdhyati
english: Then, as a cry of horror rose from the army, the kings, beholding Bhīma, said: "This is Rudra in the guise of Bhīma, hungering after the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra."

sanskrit: evam uktvāpalāyanta sarve bhārata pārthivāḥ visaṃjñāvāhayan vāhān na ca dvau saha dhāvataḥ
english: Having said this, O descendant of Bharata, all the kings fled; senseless with fear, they drove their mounts, and no two of them ran together.

sanskrit: tato bale bhṛśalulite niśāmukhe; supūjito nṛpavṛṣabhair vṛkodaraḥ mahābalaḥ kamalavibuddhalocano; yudhiṣṭhiraṃ nṛpatim apūjayad balī
english: Then, when the host had been grievously shattered at the onset of night, the mighty Vṛkodara, honored by the bulls among kings, his eyes wide as opened lotuses, in his strength paid homage to King Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: tato yamau drupadavirāṭakekayā; yudhiṣṭhiraś cāpi parāṃ mudaṃ yayuḥ vṛkodaraṃ bhṛśam abhipūjayaṃś ca te; yathāndhake pratinihate haraṃ surāḥ
english: Then the twins, Drupada, Virāṭa, the Kekayas, and Yudhiṣṭhira as well attained supreme delight, and they did high honor to Vṛkodara, as the gods honored Hara when Andhaka was slain.

sanskrit: tataḥ sutās tava varuṇātmajopamā; ruṣānvitāḥ saha guruṇā mahātmanā vṛkodaraṃ sarathapadātikuñjarā; yuyutsavo bhṛśam abhiparyavārayan
english: Then your sons, peers of the son of Varuṇa, filled with fury, together with their great-souled preceptor, eager to fight, with chariots, foot-soldiers, and elephants, closely beset Vṛkodara on every side.

sanskrit: tato 'bhavat timiraghanair ivāvṛtaṃ; mahābhaye bhayadam atīva dāruṇam niśāmukhe baḍavṛkagṛdhramodanaṃ; mahātmanāṃ nṛpavarayuddham adbhutam
english: Then, as if enveloped in dense darkness, amid great terror, fear-inspiring and exceedingly grim at the onset of night, came the gladdening feast of jackals, wolves, and vultures—the wondrous battle of the great-souled foremost of kings.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca prāyopaviṣṭe tu hate putre sātyakinā tataḥ somadatto bhṛśaṃ kruddhaḥ sātyakiṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Saṃjaya said: When his son, who had sat down to die by fasting, had been slain by Sātyaki, Somadatta, greatly enraged, spoke these words to Sātyaki:

sanskrit: kṣatradharmaḥ purā dṛṣṭo yas tu devair mahātmabhiḥ taṃ tvaṃ sātvata saṃtyajya dasyudharme kathaṃ rataḥ
english: "The duty of the warrior, ordained of old by the great-souled gods—abandoning that, O Sātvata, how is it you delight in the way of brigands?

sanskrit: parāṅmukhāya dīnāya nyastaśastrāya yācate kṣatradharmarataḥ prājñaḥ kathaṃ nu prahared raṇe
english: How could a wise man, devoted to the warrior's law, strike in battle one who has turned away, who is helpless, who has laid down his arms and begs for mercy?

sanskrit: dvāv eva kila vṛṣṇīnāṃ tatra khyātau mahārathau pradyumnaś ca mahābāhus tvaṃ caiva yudhi sātvata
english: Two only among the Vṛṣṇis, they say, are renowned as great chariot-warriors—the mighty-armed Pradyumna and you, O Sātvata, in battle.

sanskrit: kathaṃ prāyopaviṣṭāya pārthena chinnabāhave nṛśaṃsaṃ patanīyaṃ ca tādṛśaṃ kṛtavān asi
english: How could you commit so cruel and degrading a deed against one whose arm Pārtha had severed and who had sat down to die by fasting?

sanskrit: śape sātvata putrābhyām iṣṭena sukṛtena ca anatītām imāṃ rātriṃ yadi tvāṃ vīramāninam
english: I swear, O Sātvata, by my two sons, by my sacrifices and good deeds, that before this night is over—if I fail to slay you who fancy yourself a hero—

sanskrit: arakṣyamāṇaṃ pārthena jiṣṇunā sasutānujam na hanyāṃ niraye ghore pateyaṃ vṛṣṇipāṃsana
english: —unguarded by the victorious Pārtha, together with your sons and younger brothers, O disgrace of the Vṛṣṇis, then may I fall into a dreadful hell."

sanskrit: evam uktvā susaṃkruddhaḥ somadatto mahābalaḥ dadhmau śaṅkhaṃ ca tāreṇa siṃhanādaṃ nanāda ca
english: Having spoken thus, the mighty Somadatta, in great wrath, blew his conch with a piercing blast and roared a lion's roar.

sanskrit: tataḥ kamalapatrākṣaḥ siṃhadaṃṣṭro mahābalaḥ sātvato bhṛśasaṃkruddhaḥ somadattam athābravīt
english: Then the lotus-petal-eyed, lion-toothed, mighty Sātvata, greatly enraged, said this to Somadatta:

sanskrit: hato bhūriśravā vīras tava putro mahārathaḥ śalaś caiva tathā rājan bhrātṛvyasanakarśitaḥ
english: "Slain is the hero Bhūriśravas, your son, the great chariot-warrior, and Śala too, O king, worn down by grief for his brother's ruin.

sanskrit: tvāṃ cāpy adya vadhiṣyāmi saputrapaśubāndhavam tiṣṭhedānīṃ raṇe yattaḥ kauravo 'si viśeṣataḥ
english: You too I shall slay this day, together with your sons, your cattle, and your kin. Stand fast now in battle, on your guard—you are a Kaurava above all others.

sanskrit: yasmin dānaṃ damaḥ śaucam ahiṃsā hrīr dhṛtiḥ kṣamā anapāyīni sarvāṇi nityaṃ rājñi yudhiṣṭhire
english: In King Yudhiṣṭhira, charity, self-restraint, purity, non-violence, modesty, firmness, and forbearance—all these dwell forever and never depart.

sanskrit: mṛdaṅgaketos tasya tvaṃ tejasā nihataḥ purā sakarṇasaubalaḥ saṃkhye vināśaṃ samupeṣyasi
english: By the splendor of him whose banner bears the drum, you have already been slain of old; with Karṇa and the son of Subala, you shall meet your destruction in battle."

sanskrit: śape 'haṃ kṛṣṇacaraṇair iṣṭāpūrtena caiva ha yadi tvāṃ sasutaṃ pāpaṃ na hanyāṃ yudhi roṣitaḥ apayāsyasi cet tyaktvā tato mukto bhaviṣyasi
english: "I swear by the feet of Kṛṣṇa and by all my sacred works—if, roused to fury in battle, I do not slay you, you wretch, together with your son. But if you flee and quit the field, then you shall go free."

sanskrit: evam ābhāṣya cānyonyaṃ krodhasaṃraktalocanau pravṛttau śarasaṃpātaṃ kartuṃ puruṣasattamau
english: Having thus addressed each other, their eyes red with wrath, those two best of men set to work to hurl their shafts together.

sanskrit: tato gajasahasreṇa rathānām ayutena ca duryodhanaḥ somadattaṃ parivārya vyavasthitaḥ
english: Then Duryodhana, with a thousand elephants and ten thousand chariots, took his stand, surrounding Somadatta.

sanskrit: śakuniś ca susaṃkruddhaḥ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ putrapautraiḥ parivṛto bhrātṛbhiś cendravikramaiḥ syālas tava mahābāhur vajrasaṃhanano yuvā
english: And Śakuni, greatly enraged, foremost of all bearers of weapons, your mighty-armed young brother-in-law, hard as the thunderbolt, surrounded by sons and grandsons and brothers of Indra's prowess—

sanskrit: sāgraṃ śatasahasraṃ tu hayānāṃ tasya dhīmataḥ somadattaṃ maheṣvāsaṃ samantāt paryarakṣata
english: —with fully a hundred thousand horse, that wise one guarded the mighty archer Somadatta on every side.

sanskrit: rakṣyamāṇaś ca balibhiś chādayām āsa sātyakim taṃ chādyamānaṃ viśikhair dṛṣṭvā saṃnataparvabhiḥ dhṛṣṭadyumno 'bhyayāt kruddhaḥ pragṛhya mahatīṃ camūm
english: Guarded by the mighty, he covered Sātyaki with his shafts; and seeing him overwhelmed by the smooth-jointed arrows, Dhṛṣṭadyumna in wrath advanced, taking with him a great host.

sanskrit: caṇḍavātābhisṛṣṭānām udadhīnām iva svanaḥ āsīd rājan balaughānām anyonyam abhinighnatām
english: Like the roar of oceans lashed by a furious gale, O king, was the din of those floods of warriors striking down one another.

sanskrit: vivyādha somadattas tu sātvataṃ navabhiḥ śaraiḥ sātyakir daśabhiś cainam avadhīt kurupuṃgavam
english: Somadatta pierced the Sātvata with nine shafts, and Sātyaki struck that bull of the Kurus with ten.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho balavatā samare dṛḍhadhanvanā rathopasthaṃ samāsādya mumoha gatacetanaḥ
english: Deeply wounded in battle by that strong, firm-bowed warrior, he sank down upon the floor of his chariot and swooned, his senses gone.

sanskrit: taṃ vimūḍhaṃ samālakṣya sārathis tvarayānvitaḥ apovāha raṇād vīraṃ somadattaṃ mahāratham
english: Seeing him fallen senseless, his charioteer, moving with all speed, bore the hero Somadatta, that great chariot-warrior, away from the field.

sanskrit: taṃ visaṃjñaṃ samālokya yuyudhānaśarārditam drauṇir abhyadravat kruddhaḥ sātvataṃ raṇamūrdhani
english: Beholding the Sātvata senseless and tormented by Yuyudhāna's shafts, Drauṇi in wrath charged upon him at the battle's head.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ saṃprekṣya śaineyasya rathaṃ prati bhaimaseniḥ susaṃkruddhaḥ pratyamitram avārayat
english: Seeing him bearing down upon Śaineya's chariot, the son of Bhīmasena, greatly enraged, held off the foe.

sanskrit: kārṣṇāyasamayaṃ ghoram ṛkṣacarmāvṛtaṃ mahat yuktaṃ gajanibhair vāhair na hayair nāpi vā gajaiḥ
english: Terrible, wrought of black iron, vast, draped with bear-skin, yoked to mounts that resembled elephants but were neither horses nor elephants—

sanskrit: vikṣiptam aṣṭacakreṇa vivṛtākṣeṇa kūjatā dhvajenocchritatuṇḍena gṛdhrarājena rājatā
english: —set upon eight creaking wheels with gaping axles, gleaming with a banner that bore a vulture-king with uplifted beak—

sanskrit: lohitārdrapatākaṃ tam antramālāvibhūṣitam aṣṭacakrasamāyuktam āsthāya vipulaṃ ratham
english: —mounting that great chariot with its blood-wet banner, adorned with garlands of entrails and fitted with eight wheels—

sanskrit: śūlamudgaradhāriṇyā śailapādapahastayā rakṣasāṃ ghorarūpāṇām akṣauhiṇyā samāvṛtaḥ
english: —surrounded by a whole army of Rākṣasas of dreadful form, bearing spears and maces, wielding crags and trees in their hands—

sanskrit: tam udyatamahācāpaṃ niśāmya vyathitā nṛpāḥ yugāntakālasamaye daṇḍahastam ivāntakam
english: —beholding him with his great bow uplifted, the kings were dismayed, as though at the close of an age they saw Death himself, staff in hand.

sanskrit: bhayārditā pracukṣobha putrasya tava vāhinī vāyunā kṣobhitāvartā gaṅgevordhvataraṅgiṇī
english: Tormented by fear, your son's army was thrown into turmoil, like the Gaṅgā with her waves running high, her eddies churned up by the wind.

sanskrit: ghaṭotkacaprayuktena siṃhanādena bhīṣitāḥ prasusruvur gajā mūtraṃ vivyathuś ca narā bhṛśam
english: Terrified by the lion's roar that Ghaṭotkaca raised, the elephants let flow their urine, and the men were sorely shaken.

sanskrit: tato 'śmavṛṣṭir atyartham āsīt tatra samantataḥ saṃdhyākālādhikabalaiḥ pramuktā rākṣasaiḥ kṣitau
english: Then a great rain of stones fell there on every side over the earth, hurled by the Rākṣasas whose strength swells at the hour of twilight.

sanskrit: āyasāni ca cakrāṇi bhuśuṇḍyaḥ prāsatomarāḥ patanty aviralāḥ śūlāḥ śataghnyaḥ paṭṭiśās tathā
english: And iron discs, bhuśuṇḍis, javelins and lances, spears, śataghnīs, and battle-axes too fell thick and unbroken.

sanskrit: tad ugram atiraudraṃ ca dṛṣṭvā yuddhaṃ narādhipāḥ tanayās tava karṇaś ca vyathitāḥ prādravan diśaḥ
english: Seeing that fierce and exceedingly savage battle, the lords of men, your sons, and Karṇa, shaken, fled in all directions.

sanskrit: tatraiko 'strabalaślāghī drauṇir mānī na vivyathe vyadhamac ca śarair māyāṃ ghaṭotkacavinirmitām
english: There alone the proud Drauṇi, glorying in the might of his weapons, was not shaken, and with his shafts he scattered the illusion wrought by Ghaṭotkaca.

sanskrit: nihatāyāṃ tu māyāyām amarṣī sa ghaṭotkacaḥ visasarja śarān ghorāṃs te 'śvatthāmānam āviśan
english: When his illusion was destroyed, the wrathful Ghaṭotkaca let fly dreadful shafts, and they fell upon Aśvatthāman.

sanskrit: bhujagā iva vegena valmīkaṃ krodhamūrchitāḥ te śarā rudhirābhyaktā bhittvā śāradvatīsutam viviśur dharaṇīṃ śīghrā rukmapuṅkhāḥ śilāśitāḥ
english: Like serpents frenzied with rage rushing into an anthill, those swift, gold-feathered, stone-whetted shafts, smeared with blood, pierced the son of Śāradvatī and plunged into the earth.
